dataset.name: Typha angustifolia non-destructive biomass data from an upland tidal brackish marsh, PIE LTER, Byfield, MA, (2022-2024)
description: This dataset contains non-destructive measurements of key features of Typha angustifolia samples. These samples were measured during the growing season in 2022, 2023, and 2024 in an upland brackish tidal wetland along the Parker River, Byfield, Massachusetts (MA), which is within the Plum Island Ecosystems Long Term Ecological Research Station (PIE LTER). Measurements were taken to investigate the difference in above ground biomass between two locations, the marsh interior (MI) and the creek bank (CB) and to support an allometric equation used to predict aboveground Typha angustifolia biomass per square meter. No QA/QC procedures were applied to the data. Metadata files Typha_biomass_observations_dd.csv and Typha_biomass_observations_flmd.csv contain detailed information on variable definitions, sampling methods, and the location of the site.

spatialCoverage.description: Ameriflux site US-PLo, Newbury, MA, established May 2022. It is a brackish tidal wetland located in the upper estuary of the Parker River, dominated by Typha angustifolia. The site includes two subsites: Marsh Interior (MI) and Creek Bank (CB). These differ in proximity to the river, with Creek Bank located closer to the river and therefore experiencing higher salinity.

measurementTechnique: Measurements were taken once a month from June to October 2022. Before the first measurements were taken, six plots were established and marked with PVC pipe, three in the marsh interior (MI) subsite and three in the creek bank (CB) subsite. Within each plot, three new plant shoots were tagged prior to the first sample in June. Each month and for each tagged plant, the presence of flowering and evidence of senescence were observed and recorded. Then, the diameter of the plant’s culm and another culm measurement perpendicular to the first one were measured and recorded along with an average of these two measurements. The total number of leaves, the number of brown leaves, and the number of green leaves were also counted and recorded. If green leaves were present, two heights of the tallest green leaf were measured and recorded: the ground to tip height of the green part of the leaf, and then the total ground to tip height of the leaf, including the brown tip. If the plant contained a flower, two additional height measurements were taken: the ground to tip height of the green part of the flower stem and the ground to tip total height of the stem, including the brown tip. Finally, the total number of green stems present in the plot were counted.
